notes: Pre-cutoff most-recent 20-F. The FY2024 20-F was filed 2024-12-05 (post-cutoff) so excluded. The ARQQ narrative is light on named Pentagon Program Elements: the company is a UK-domiciled symmetric-key SaaS vendor with channel partners (Juniper, Fortinet, AWS, Sierra Nevada Mission Systems UK, DETASAD, Carahsoft) and only commercial customers explicitly named (BT plc, AUCloud, Nine23). Defense exposure is positioned indirectly via NSA Commercial Solutions for Classified (CSfC) alignment, US National Security Memorandum 10 (NSM-10) framing, and channel-partner reach into defense buyers. We extract J-Book-grounded claims to test whether ARQQ's load-bearing forward narrative depends on Pentagon program revenue that the J-Book corpus would have foreseen as not arriving.

claims.claim_text: Arqit's symmetric key agreement platform is compliant with the NSA Commercial Solutions for Classified (CSfC) Symmetric Key Management Requirements Annex (version 1.2 / 2.1), positioning it for U.S. government classified-network adoption.
claims.subject: Arqit QuantumCloud / Symmetric Key Agreement platform
claims.object_value: NSA CSfC Symmetric Key Management Requirements Annex v1.2 / v2.1
claims.source_quote: Arqit believes that its symmetric key agreement platform is compliant with the NSA Commercial Solutions for Classified Symmetric Key Management Requirements Annex 1.2 ... Arqit's Symmetric Key Agreement platform delivers encryption in a manner that meets the demands of US National Security Memorandum 10 and National Security Agency Commercial Solutions for Classified Symmetric Key Management Requirements Annex version 2.1.

claims.claim_text: Arqit asserts that the White House National Security Memorandum 10 (NSM-10, May 4 2022) sets a deadline of end-2023 for government agencies to ensure quantum-safe security for National Security Systems, and 'has made it clear that adoption of symmetric key protections for NSS is the preferred solution' — framed as a regulatory driver of forward demand.
claims.subject: U.S. federal agencies / National Security Systems
claims.object_value: symmetric-key quantum-safe protections by end-2023 per NSM-10
claims.source_quote: The memorandum sets a crucial deadline for government agencies ensuring quantum-safe security for National Security Systems by the end of 2023... Memorandum 10 has made it clear that adoption of symmetric key protections for NSS is the preferred solution.

claims.claim_text: Arqit has announced channel-partnership / distribution agreements with Sierra Nevada Corporation Mission Systems UK, DETASAD, and Carahsoft — vendors that route to defense / government end-customers — through which it 'will sell directly and indirectly to end customers'.
claims.subject: Arqit channel-partner network
claims.object_value: Sierra Nevada Corp Mission Systems UK, DETASAD, Carahsoft (gov/defense reseller)
claims.source_quote: Arqit has announced channel partnerships and distribution agreements with Juniper, Fortinet, AWS, TraxPay, Exclusive Networks, Sierra Nevada Corporation Mission Systems UK, SecureCloud+, DETASAD, Advanced International Electronic Equipment Company, and Carahsoft through which it will sell directly and indirectly to end customers.

claims.claim_text: Arqit is positioned to meet 'the demands of US National Security Memorandum 10' and represents 'the only commercially available symmetric key encryption system which is the preferred cryptographic architecture of both NIST and The White House' — a forward-revenue narrative anchored on U.S. federal quantum-safe adoption.
claims.subject: Arqit (vs. PQC alternatives)
claims.source_quote: Unlike solutions utilizing Post-Quantum Cryptographic Algorithms proposed by other parties, Arqit believes it has the only commercially available symmetric key encryption system which is the preferred cryptographic architecture of both NIST and The White House.

claims.claim_text: Arqit announced it will focus on selling its products on a Platform-as-a-Service basis primarily through channel partners and distributors, which is 'expected to generate annual recurring revenue' — i.e., a forward revenue thesis materially dependent on channel reach into defense / classified buyers.
claims.subject: Arqit forward revenue model
claims.source_quote: Arqit announced in December 2022 that it will focus on selling its products on a Platform as a Service basis, primarily through channel partners and distributors, which is expected to generate annual recurring revenue.

claims.claim_text: Arqit announced (May 2023) it had retained an adviser to pursue the sale of its satellite division (assets, patents, customer contracts, engineering team); a $17.6m impairment of the satellite intangible was recorded for FY2023 and the asset was reclassified as held-for-sale ($38.7m intangible held for sale).
claims.subject: Arqit satellite division
claims.object_value: $17.6m impairment; $38.7m intangible reclassified as held for sale; sale process initiated
claims.source_quote: An impairment of $17.6 million was deemed necessary for the satellite ... Arqit announced that through innovation in the delivery of its products, quantum satellite hardware was no longer required and that it intends to monetise (in whole or in part as a capacity sharing arrangement) its quantum satellite currently under construction.

claims.claim_text: Arqit's symmetric-key protocol security proofs were 'independently assured in 2022 by the University of Surrey, which is accredited as a Centre of Excellence for Cyber Security by the UK Government's National Cyber Security Centre' — a credibility claim used to anchor the technology-validation narrative.
claims.subject: Arqit symmetric-key protocols
claims.object_value: University of Surrey (NCSC-accredited Centre of Excellence)
claims.source_quote: The security proofs for the design aspects of the key-establishment protocols used to enable symmetric key agreement over classical IP network infrastructures within QuantumCloud TM were independently assured in 2022 by the University of Surrey, which is accredited as a Centre of Excellence for Cyber Security by the UK Government s National Cyber Security Centre.

claims.claim_text: Arqit's stated cash balance was $44m as at Sep-30-2023 (vs $49m FY22, $87m FY21); FY23 cash used in operating activities was $32.8m and the directors expressed a going-concern view that the cash was 'sufficient to enable the Group to grow according to its plans' — a forward-survival claim that is load-bearing for the defense-revenue narrative.
claims.subject: Arqit Quantum Inc.
claims.object_value: $44m cash at FY23 end vs ~$33m/yr operating burn
claims.source_quote: Following the close of the business combination transaction in September 2021 the Company had $87m as at 30 September 2021, $49m as at 30 September 2022, and $44m as at 30 September 2023. Based on business forecasts, this is sufficient to enable the Group to grow according to its plans.
